review: The hymn is Philippians 3:7–14 and Ephesians 1:4: 1:1–4 is Eph 1:4 (בָּחַר … לִפְנֵי מוֹסְדוֹת תֵּבֵל) with 1 Pet 1:20, 2:1–4 Phil 3:14 with Eph 1:18, 3:1–4 Phil 3:7–8 (כִּי הַכֹּל חֵפֶץ לִי … לְמַעַן אַרְוִיחַ אֶת־הַמָּשִׁיחַ), 4:1–4 Phil 3:12–13 with Heb 11:13, and 5:1–4 Phil 1:21–23 with John 14:2.

3:2 אַךְ־הֶבֶל וּרְעוּת רוּחַ — the Arabic نُفَايَةٌ وَقَبْضُ رِيح is 'refuse and the grasping of wind'; the Hebrew uses the doubled idiom of Ecclesiastes (הֶבֶל וּרְעוּת רוּחַ), because the stanza is making Qohelet's judgement and not merely listing two insults.

3:3–4 אֶשְׁכַּל כָּל־קִנְיָנַי / אֶקְנֶה אֶת־הַמָּשִׁיחַ — the Arabic وَإِنْ خَسِرْتُ كُلَّ شَيْ / فَذَا لِأَرْبَحَ الْمَسِيح keeps the commercial metaphor of gain and loss; the Hebrew reproduces it with the cognate pair שָׁכַל/קָנָה, so the loss and the gain are one transaction and the line sounds like a bill of sale, as Paul's does.

2:2 גְּבֹהָה מִדַּעַת כֹּל — the Arabic تَفُوقُ إِدْرَاكَ الْمَلَا is 'surpassing the comprehension of the hosts', i.e. of the angels; the Hebrew uses the collective כֹּל rather than מַלְאָכִים, because the line is short and the point is that the calling outruns every creature's understanding, not that angels specifically were consulted.

6:4 בְּמוֹלַדְתִּי לָנֶצַח — the Arabic فِي مَوْطِنِي إِلَى الْأَبَد is 'in my homeland forever'; the Hebrew uses מוֹלֶדֶת, the land of one's birth (Gen 12:1, מֵאֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתְּךָ), so the last line closes the exile-language of 4:1 (גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב) with the return home.
